Section: Leave
## Purpose The Annual Leave Policy explains how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward. It applies to full-time employees unless a different written employment agreement applies. ## Annual Leave Entitlement Full-time employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave during each calendar year. The annual leave year runs from January through December. Employees joining during the year may receive a proportional entitlement based on their employment start date. Annual leave is intended to provide employees with time away from work for rest and personal activities. Employees should plan their leave throughout the year rather than waiting until the final weeks of December. ## Requesting Annual Leave Employees should normally submit annual leave requests at least 10 working days before the requested start date. Requests must be submitted through the approved company leave system. The employee should include the requested start date, end date and any information needed by the manager to understand operational impact. Employees should not make non-refundable travel arrangements before receiving approval when the leave depends on manager authorization. Emergency circumstances may prevent an employee from providing 10 working days of notice. Managers may consider shorter notice where reasonable. ## Manager Approval Managers approve annual leave based on staffing levels, customer commitments, project deadlines and operational requirements. Submitting a leave request does not automatically mean that the leave has been approved. Managers should try to accommodate reasonable requests while ensuring that the team can

title: Customer Billing Cycle Policy

Title: Customer Billing Cycle Policy
Section: Billing
Monthly subscriptions are billed on the customer's recurring billing date. Annual subscriptions are billed once at the beginning of each annual subscription period. Failed payments may be retried automatically before an account is suspended. Billing frequency is separate from the published monthly subscription price.

title: Business Travel Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Business Travel Policy
Section: Travel
Business travel should be booked using approved suppliers whenever possible. Employees should select reasonably priced transport and accommodation suitable for the business requirement. International travel requires manager approval before booking. Travel costs must later be submitted under the Employee Expense Policy.

title: Corporate Card Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Corporate Card Policy
Section: Corporate Cards
Corporate cards may only be used for authorized business expenses. Personal purchases are prohibited. Cardholders must retain receipts and reconcile transactions by the monthly Finance deadline. Lost or stolen cards must be reported immediately to Finance and the card provider.

title: Customer Onboarding Process

Section: Onboarding
New customers receive a welcome email after their account has been activated. Customer Success schedules an onboarding session to review account configuration, user setup and key product features. Professional and Enterprise customers may receive additional implementation assistance depending on their agreement. The account owner confirms onboarding completion after agreed setup activities have been completed.

Title: Customer Refund Policy
Section: Refunds
## Purpose The Customer Refund Policy defines when customers may request refunds, what evidence is required and how approved refunds are processed. This policy should be used when deciding refund eligibility. Other documents may describe returns, payment processing or customer-service terminology, but those documents do not replace this policy. ## Standard Refund Period Customers may request a full refund within 30 calendar days of the original purchase date. The 30-day period begins on the date shown on the customer's valid purchase record. Requests submitted within this period are reviewed according to the eligibility requirements described in this policy. A request made after 30 calendar days is not automatically eligible for a refund. ## Proof of Purchase Customers must provide a valid order number or another acceptable form of proof of purchase. Customer Operations may use account records to verify a transaction when appropriate. If the company cannot confirm that the purchase occurred, the refund request may be delayed while additional evidence is requested. ## Eligible Refunds A refund may be approved when the request falls within the applicable period and the purchase satisfies the relevant product or service conditions. For physical products, the separate Product Returns Policy may also apply. Returning an item does not automatically guarantee refund approval. Refund eligibility remains governed by this Customer Refund Policy. ## Requests After 30 Days Refund requests received after the 30-day period are reviewed individually. Customer Operations may consider exceptional circumstances, but

title: Confidential Data Handling Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Confidential Data Handling Policy
Section: Data Protection
Confidential company and customer information must only be stored in approved systems. Employees must not send confidential data to personal email accounts or unauthorized cloud storage services. Access should be limited to people who need the information for legitimate business purposes. Suspected data exposure must be reported under the Security Incident Reporting process.

title: Employee Expense Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Employee Expense Policy
Section: Expenses
The company reimburses reasonable and approved business expenses including travel, accommodation and customer meeting costs. Expense claims must be submitted within 14 calendar days of the expense being incurred. Receipts must be attached to claims whenever available. Managers are responsible for confirming that expenses are reasonable and business-related before approval.

title: Employee Onboarding Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Employee Onboarding Policy
Section: Employee Onboarding
New employees complete company orientation during their first working week. Onboarding includes account setup, required security training, department introduction and review of relevant company policies. The employee's manager is responsible for confirming role-specific onboarding activities. Information Technology creates approved system accounts after receiving the required onboarding request.

title: Lead Qualification Guide
embedding_text:
Title: Lead Qualification Guide
Section: Lead Qualification
Sales representatives should confirm customer need, appropriate business fit, expected timing and a realistic purchasing process before treating a lead as qualified. Unqualified enquiries may remain in the CRM for future nurturing. Qualification does not mean that a sale has been completed. Only signed agreements may be treated as completed sales.

title: Mandatory Employee Training
embedding_text:
Title: Mandatory Employee Training
Section: Training
Employees must complete required compliance and information-security training within the assigned deadline. New employees receive mandatory training assignments during onboarding. Managers are responsible for following up when required training becomes overdue. Additional role-specific training may be required by individual departments.

title: Parental Leave Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Parental Leave Policy
Section: Leave
Eligible employees may request parental leave following the birth, adoption or placement of a child. Employees should contact Human Resources at least eight weeks before the expected leave start date where reasonably possible. Individual entitlement and payment arrangements depend on employment terms and applicable local requirements. Parental leave is managed separately from the standard annual leave allowance.

title: Password Security Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Password Security Policy
Section: Authentication
Employees must use strong and unique passwords for company systems. Multi-factor authentication is required where the company system supports it. Passwords must never be shared with colleagues or external parties. Suspected password compromise must be reported immediately to Information Security.

title: Pricing and Discount Rules
embedding_text:
Title: Pricing and Discount Rules
Section: Discounts
Sales representatives may offer approved promotional discounts only within the limits defined by the Commercial team. Discounts above 10 percent require approval from a sales manager. Enterprise contract discounts are considered individually and may require Finance approval. Employees must not promise customers an unapproved discount.

title: Subscription Pricing
embedding_text:
Title: Subscription Pricing
Section: Pricing
The Standard Plan costs $49 per month and supports up to five users. The Professional Plan costs $99 per month and supports up to 15 users. Enterprise pricing is customized according to user numbers, integrations, support requirements and contract terms. Customers interested in Enterprise pricing must request a quotation from the sales team.

title: Product Returns Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Product Returns Policy
Section: Returns
Physical products may be returned within 30 calendar days when they are unused and in resalable condition. Customers must obtain a return reference before shipping an item back to the company. Receiving a returned product does not automatically mean that a refund has been approved. Refund eligibility is governed by the separate Customer Refund Policy.

title: Purchase Order Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Purchase Order Policy
Section: Purchase Orders
A valid purchase order must normally be issued before a supplier provides goods or services. The purchase order should identify the supplier, approved amount, business owner and relevant cost allocation. Employees should not personally commit the company to unauthorized supplier expenditure. Exceptions require documented approval under the procurement process.

title: Customer Service Vocabulary Training

Section: Training Examples
This training document teaches customer-service vocabulary. Employees may encounter words such as refund, return, payment, money back, billing, purchase and customer complaint during support conversations. The document contains examples of common customer language but does not define refund eligibility, return periods or company payment rules. Employees must use the official Customer Refund Policy when answering questions about refund eligibility.

title: Refund Processing Guide
embedding_text:
Title: Refund Processing Guide
Section: Payment Processing
Once Customer Operations approves a refund, Finance processes the payment through the original payment channel. Most approved refunds reach the customer within five to seven working days, although bank processing times may vary. Finance employees should not approve refund eligibility themselves. title: Remote Work Equipment Guidelines

Title: Remote Work Equipment Guidelines
Section: Equipment
Employees approved for remote work may receive a company laptop, headset and other equipment required for their role. Company equipment remains the property of Northstar Systems and must be used in accordance with security policies. Employees must report lost, stolen or damaged equipment to the IT service desk as soon as possible. The equipment policy does not determine how many days an employee is permitted to work remotely.

title: Sales Contract Approval Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Sales Contract Approval Policy
Section: Contract Approval
Standard contracts using approved commercial terms may follow the normal sales approval process. Non-standard legal terms must be reviewed by the appropriate legal reviewer before signature. Large discounts, unusual payment terms or significant commercial exceptions may require Finance or senior management approval. A sales opportunity must not be recorded as Closed Won before required signatures are complete.

title: Sales Opportunity Process
embedding_text:
Title: Sales Opportunity Process
Section: Opportunity Management
Qualified sales opportunities must be recorded in the company CRM. Sales representatives must update the opportunity stage when meaningful progress occurs. An opportunity may only be marked Closed Won after the customer has signed the required sales agreement. Lost opportunities should include a loss reason to support future sales analysis.

title: Security Incident Reporting
embedding_text:
Title: Security Incident Reporting
Section: Incident Management
Employees must immediately report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorized system access or data exposure. Reports should be submitted through the security incident channel or IT service desk. Employees should not attempt to investigate serious security incidents independently. Information Security coordinates investigation, containment and recovery activities.

title: Sick Leave Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Sick Leave Policy
Section: Leave
Employees who are unable to work because of illness must notify their manager before their normal starting time whenever reasonably possible. Medical documentation may be required for absences lasting more than three consecutive working days. Sick leave must not be recorded as annual leave unless Human Resources specifically approves the change.

title: Supplier Payment Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Supplier Payment Policy
Section: Supplier Payments
Approved supplier invoices are normally paid according to the payment terms stated in the supplier agreement. Finance requires a valid invoice and appropriate purchasing approval before payment. Invoice discrepancies should be resolved with Procurement or the relevant business owner. Supplier payment processing does not replace purchase-order approval requirements.

title: Supplier Selection Policy
embedding_text:
Title: Supplier Selection Policy
Section: Supplier Selection
New suppliers must be evaluated for capability, commercial suitability and relevant risk before approval. Purchases above $10,000 normally require comparison of at least three suitable supplier quotations unless an approved exception applies. Procurement records the selection decision and supporting evidence. Employees must disclose potential conflicts of interest involving prospective suppliers.

title: Support Escalation Process
embedding_text:
Title: Support Escalation Process
Section: Escalations
Support agents should escalate cases when customer impact increases, agreed troubleshooting does not resolve the issue or specialist expertise is required. Critical incidents are escalated immediately to the designated incident lead. Escalation does not change the original support priority unless the impact assessment also changes. Major customer-impacting incidents may require updates to Customer Success and senior management.

title: Customer Support Service Levels
embedding_text:
Title: Customer Support Service Levels
Section: Service Levels
Critical support incidents receive an initial response within one hour during supported business hours. High-priority requests receive an initial response within four hours. Normal-priority requests receive an initial response within one business day. Response targets describe the initial acknowledgement and investigation start, not guaranteed resolution time.
